gaps.explanation: 'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

gaps.sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
gaps.hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
gaps.explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.

gaps.sentence: These shoes were ___ made for the customer.
gaps.explanation: 'Specially' means for a particular purpose ('specially made'); 'especially' means in particular.

gaps.sentence: The storm did considerable ___ to the harbour wall.
gaps.explanation: 'Do damage' — uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded in court.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.
'Besides' means in addition to; 'beside' means next to; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: The children left ___ toys all over the floor.
gaps.explanation: 'Their' shows possession; 'there' is a place; 'they're' means 'they are'; 'theirs' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.
